newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Gov sees no 'incremental' progress on budget.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Gov sees no 'incremental' progress on budget.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki said Tuesday he and Albany lawmakers made no progress toward reaching a new budget for fiscal 1998 one week before a short legislative recess.

"As I said the other day, we are not even making yet making incremental progress on the budget but we will continue to try," Pataki told reporters in Albany. The state's budget was due on April 1, and last year it failed to approve a new pact until 104 days after the deadline.

Pataki declined to discuss the specifics of one of the logjams -- the June 15 expiry of rent contrals -- though he again put himself forward as a potential deal-maker, noting his Administration had negotiated a difficult pact with upstate communities to protect New York City's reservoir system.
The rent rules mainly affect New York City residents, as there are nearly one million rent-regulated apartments in the city.

Asked if New York City Mayor Rudloph Guiliani had made progress in resolving the issue in talks on Monday with Albany lawmakers, Pataki said: "I think there is a willingness to reach common ground, and I think that's a very important first step."

Pataki also made it plain that the battle over rent controls was not the only fight, saying the state needed a "soundly balanced" budget that included his welform and criminal justice proposals, as well as school tax relief.

Senate Majority Leader, Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, wants rent rules ended in two years for all but the disabled, needy and elderly, while the Assembly Speaker, Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, wants them extended.
Pataki has repeatedly attacked the Assembly for wanting to raise spending by too much in its own version of a budget, though it forecasts signifcantly higher revenues than the governor.
